title: PageTurn Book V3
summary: A framework-neutral semantic book reader and publication library that keeps text as native HTML while adding page-turn geometry, for publishing scholarly books and reports on the web.

narrative.problem: Fixed-page book viewers rasterize publication text, which costs native, accessible and searchable HTML and durable links to individual passages. Scholarly publications need a reader that still turns like a book while keeping text semantic and citable.
narrative.decision: Publications are compiled from metadata and Markdown into immutable manifests and directly readable chapter HTML; the reader loads only a bounded current and adjacent chapter window and projects StPageFlip-derived page-turn geometry onto accessible semantic page faces.
narrative.tradeoff: Keeping text as live HTML preserves accessibility, search and durable source anchors, but every book must go through the publication compiler, and the older V2 reader and V1 fixed-page viewer are kept as compatibility paths that still need testing.
narrative.limitation: Public npm registry publication is blocked until the project license is approved, so consumers must build and install a tarball; quote sharing, share composing and external previews stay off unless the host supplies an explicit policy.
